gap: No result ChatGPT got gives today's maker-store prices. The 2,048 Wh / 2,400 W+ class that can run an 1,800 W induction plate starts at $879 (EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max, in stock) and $899 (BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, 2,600 W, in stock). It does not start at the $1,499–$1,999 ChatGPT showed. The BLUETTI AC200L it listed at $1,999 is $899 on BLUETTI's store and out of stock.
standout_why: Checked the cited bluettipower.com/pages/ac200l: it gives specs (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, 7,200 W surge, 62.4 lb, 20 A outlets) with no price or stock, and never mentions induction cooking. The cited unpluggedwatts.com comparison failed to load twice with an SSL certificate error, so I can't say whether it prints prices. ChatGPT's own answer shows $1,499 / $879 / $1,999 with no dates or sellers. Its $1,999 for the AC200L is more than twice BLUETTI's $899 list price, and it doesn't flag that the AC200L is out of stock.
decides: The price changes the pick. Two in-stock 2 kWh units with headroom over an 1,800 W plate cost about $880–$900 at the maker. These are the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max ($879, 2,400 W) and the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 ($899, 2,600 W, ours). At that price, ChatGPT's $1,499 Anker C2000 Gen 2 top pick is hard to justify. The out-of-stock, 62.4 lb AC200L drops out. The DELTA 2 Max ($1,029) matches the DELTA 3 Max on capacity and output but costs $150 more. The $549 AC180 and $649 DELTA 3 Plus are rated at 1,800 W, exactly what a full-power 1,800 W plate draws. They only make sense with a 1,500 W-or-lower cooktop. Our current page is stale: it shows the AC180 as 'back late Nov' and the DELTA 3 Plus at $719 on pre-order. Today both are in stock, at $549 and $649.
